column3: The Hebrew repeats “with you” rather than saying “alone” in the second clause.
The Hebrew distinguishes the Levites’ serving Aaron from Aaron and his sons being before the Tent.
The Hebrew does not add “the sanctuary” after the outsider’s coming near.
The Hebrew says it shall be holy to you, rather than explicitly commanding you to regard it as holy.
The Hebrew uses the image of fat for the best of the oil, wine, and grain; it does not specify freshness.
The Hebrew directly commands Aaron to redeem the ones to be redeemed, without an explicit verb for paying.
The Hebrew first names the Levite in the singular, then uses the plural.
The Hebrew explicitly says the LORD spoke to Moses, saying.
The Hebrew joins the two comparisons with “and” and calls the winepress produce its fullness.
The Hebrew calls the best part its fat.
The Hebrew says it will be reckoned to the Levites and joins the two comparisons with “and”.
